summary: @onereach/or-browser-next preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall script (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (oven-sh/bun), extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and then invokes it against `math_init.js`, a 727 KB single-line JavaScript file shipped in the tarball that is heavily obfuscated with a rotating string-array and hex-named identifiers over a custom decoder alphabet. Before the download, setup.mjs fingerprints the host by running `ldd --version` and reading `/etc/os-release` to detect musl/Alpine and by combining `process.platform` and `process.arch` to select one of six platform-specific Bun binaries (linux-x64/arm64 glibc and musl, darwin-x64/arm64, win32-x64/arm64), so the install-time execution succeeds uniformly on Linux, macOS, and Windows developer and CI hosts. If Bun is already present on PATH it is invoked directly. The package presents itself as a Vue UI component for browsing files; that stated purpose does not require an alternate language runtime or an obfuscated blob, and the payload's contents are hidden from Node-based tooling because they only execute inside the fetched Bun binary. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper shape: at `npm install` time the package fetches a separate runtime and uses it to execute an opaque, obfuscated payload bundled in the tarball.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
